extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates, graduate students, and researchers studying category theory (monads and algebras)
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and formal development of monads, T-algebras, Kleisli and Eilenberg–Moore constructions, examples (groups, modules, words), split coequalizers, and Beck's theorem characterizing monadicity. Includes definitions, constructions, comparison theorems and illustrative examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monad (definition via endofunctor, unit, multiplication)
rubrics_metrics.description: A monad in X is given by an endofunctor T: X -> X together with natural transformations η: 1 -> T (unit) and μ: T^2 -> T (multiplication) such that the associative diagram and the left and right unit diagrams commute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogy: replace the set M of a monoid by endofunctor T, product by composition, unit element by identity endofunctor; μ plays multiplication and η the unit. The three commutative diagrams (associativity, left unit, right unit) are the monad laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monad arising from an adjunction
rubrics_metrics.description: Every adjunction (F, G, η, ε): X ⇄ A yields a monad in X with T = G F, unit η the unit of the adjunction, and multiplication μ = G ε F: G F G F -> G F = T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the monad laws by translating the triangular identities and the interchange law for functors/natural transformations; diagrams showing commutativity follow from properties of the adjunction (e.g., composition of G e F yields μ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comonad (dual notion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dually, a comonad in a category consists of a functor L and natural transformations Δ: L -> L^2 and ε: L -> I which render the dual comultiplicative and counit diagrams commutative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every adjunction (F, G, η, ε): X ⇄ A also defines a comonad (FG, ε, FηG) in A by dual construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monad in a preorder equals closure operation
rubrics_metrics.description: If P is a preorder, a monad T: P -> P is a monotone function satisfying x ≤ Tx and T(Tx) ≤ Tx for all x; in a partial order these equations imply T(Tx) = Tx, so a monad is precisely a closure operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret natural transformations η and μ as the inequalities x ≤ Tx and T(Tx) ≤ Tx respectively; uniqueness of arrows in preorders forces diagrams to commute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphism of monads (prompted)
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism of monads <T, η, μ> -> <T', η', μ'> is a suitable natural transformation θ: T -> T' compatible with units and multiplications (left for the reader to describe).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text leaves explicit construction to the reader; in practice θ must satisfy θ ∘ η = η' and θ ∘ μ = μ' ∘ (θ * θ) (compatibility with multiplication), yielding a category of monads on X.

rubrics_metrics.name: T-algebra (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a monad T = (T, η, μ) in X, a T-algebra is a pair (x, h) with x ∈ X and h: T x -> x such that the associative diagram (h ∘ μ_x = h ∘ T h) and unit diagram (h ∘ η_x = id_x) commute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think of a T-algebra as an object on which the 'monoid' T acts; the two commuting diagrams are exactly the algebra laws (associativity and unit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms of T-algebras
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism f: (x,h) -> (x',h') of T-algebras is an arrow f: x -> x' in X making the square f ∘ h = h' ∘ T f commute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures f is compatible with the algebra structures; composition of such morphisms yields the category X^T of T-algebras.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category X^T and adjunction FT ⊣ GT
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of all T-algebras and their morphisms form a category X^T. There is an adjunction FT ⊣ GT where GT: X^T -> X forgets structure and FT: X -> X^T sends x to the free algebra (T x, μ_x). The monad defined by this adjunction is the original T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GT FT x = T x, the unit of the given monad is the adjunction unit, and counit e_T at (x,h) is h. Verify triangular identities from algebra laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free T-algebra on x
rubrics_metrics.description: The free T-algebra on x ∈ X is (T x, μ_x), where μ_x: T^2 x -> T x is the multiplication component at x; FT(x) = (T x, μ_x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows because the monad laws ensure (T x, μ_x) satisfies the algebra diagrams; FT is left adjoint to the forgetful functor GT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example: closure algebras and complete semilattices (~-algebras)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the covariant power-set functor ~ on Set with η_x: x ↦ {x} and μ_x union, (~, η, μ) is a monad; a ~-algebra (X,h) corresponds exactly to a complete semilattice with sup given by h.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises guide verifying (~, η, μ) is a monad and that its algebras are precisely (small) complete semilattices with sup-preserving morphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example: group actions as algebras for G×(-) monad
rubrics_metrics.description: For a group G, the functor T X = G × X with unit and multiplication defined by group unit and multiplication yields a monad on Set; a T-algebra is exactly a G-set (a set X with an action G × X -> X satisfying action axioms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate the algebra conditions h∘η = id and h∘μ = h∘T h into the usual G-action properties g1(g2 x) = (g1 g2) x and 1 x = x.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example: R-modules as algebras for R⊗(-) monad
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ring R, the functor T A = R ⊗ A on Ab with unit and multiplication induced by R yields a monad whose T-algebras are exactly left R-modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure map h assigns to a pure tensor r ⊗ a the scalar multiple r·a; checking algebra diagrams recovers module axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word (free semigroup) monad W and its algebras
rubrics_metrics.description: The word monad W on Set has W X = disjoint union of X^n (words of positive length), unit sending x to one-letter word (x), and μ removing nested brackets; W-algebras correspond to sets equipped with operations V_n (one for each arity n) satisfying identities including V1 = id and coherence (equation (2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition: W-algebras are algebraic systems with one n-ary operation V_n for each n, with V1 = identity and compatibility identities ensuring V_n are iterates of a binary associative operation when applicable; this recovers semigroups when V2 is associative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kleisli category construction (XT) for a monad
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a monad (T, η, μ) in X, form a category X_T with objects x_T (one per x ∈ X) and arrows f': x_T -> y_T corresponding bijectively to arrows f: x -> T y in X. Composition f' ◦ g' is defined using x -> T y -> T^2 z -> T z (via T g then μ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define FT: X -> X_T by FT(x)=x_T and FT(k)= (η_y ∘ k)' etc., and GT: X_T -> X by mapping f' to T y ∘ f; these give an adjunction FT ⊣ GT recovering the monad. Verify associativity and unit by diagram chases using μ and η.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison functor K: A -> X^T and monadicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an adjunction (F,G,η,ε): X ⇄ A with monad T = (G F, η, G ε F), there is a unique functor K: A -> X^T with G^T K = G and K F = F^T. If K is an isomorphism (or equivalence), G is called monadic (or tripleable/triplable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: K is built by sending a ∈ A to (G a, G ε_a : G F G a -> G a) as T-algebra. Examples: For Set ⇄ Top (discrete functor D left adjoint to forgetful G) the monad is identity and K equals G (not necessarily iso).

rubrics_metrics.name: Split fork and split coequalizer (definition and properties)
rubrics_metrics.description: A split fork is a fork a ⇉^s_b -> c with additional arrows s: c -> b and t: b -> a satisfying e s = id_c, s 0 = id and the equations e∘s = id_c, α∘t = id_a, β∘t = s∘e (see (2),(3)). In any split fork e is the coequalizer of the parallel pair and is an absolute coequalizer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Split forks remain split under any functor, so split coequalizers are absolute. Examples: in Cat and Grp (quotient constructions) forks become split after applying forgetful functors to Set by choosing sections/representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma: Split fork implies coequalizer
rubrics_metrics.description: In every split fork, the arrow e is a coequalizer of the parallel pair α, β; proof via factorization through the section s (take f' = f s) and uniqueness from e s = id.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shows split coequalizers provide canonical factorization of maps equalizing α and β; being defined only by composites and identities, split forks are preserved by any functor (hence absolute).

rubrics_metrics.name: Beck's theorem (characterization of algebras / monadicity)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an adjunction (F,G,η,ε): X ⇄ A with monad T and comparison K: A -> X^T, the following are equivalent: (i) K is an isomorphism; (ii) G creates coequalizers for those parallel pairs f,g in A for which Gf,Gg have an absolute coequalizer in X; (iii) G creates coequalizers for those parallel pairs f,g in A for which Gf,Gg have a split coequalizer in X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof sketch: (i)⇒(ii) by constructing algebra structure on the coequalizer z in X using absoluteness to lift Tz; (ii)⇒(iii) trivial since split implies absolute; (iii)⇒(i) via canonical presentations (forks FGFG a ⇉ FG a -> a), applying G yields split forks in X which G must create, producing a unique comparison and showing K is iso. This is the 'precise tripleability theorem' (PTT); many variants (weak, equivalence, constructive, crude VTT/CTT) exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical presentation (fork) for an object in A
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ∈ A the adjunction provides a canonical fork FGFG a ⇉ FG a -> a (with maps coming from counit), called the canonical presentation of a; applying G yields a split fork in X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fork is used in Beck's theorem: when G creates the coequalizer of its image (a split coequalizer), uniqueness and existence of comparisons follow. In algebraic categories this is analogous to presenting an object by generators and relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and uniqueness of comparison functors under coequalizer hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: If G satisfies the hypothesis of creating coequalizers for the relevant split/absolute pairs, then the comparison functor M (or K) between adjunctions or to X^T is uniquely determined and yields isomorphisms when both directions are constructed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The uniqueness argument uses that the image under G of the canonical presentation is a split fork and hence has a uniquely determined coequalizer in A when G creates it; this determines M on objects and arrows, and functoriality follows from factorization uniqueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflection of colimits by a functor G
rubrics_metrics.description: G: A -> X reflects colimits of a diagram T: J -> A when any cone e: T -> a whose image G e is colimiting in X is already colimiting in A; in particular G reflects coequalizers when forks becoming coequalizers in X were already coequalizers in A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflection is used in stronger forms of Beck-like theorems: if G both creates and reflects certain colimits (or reflects isomorphisms) then stronger monadicity/equivalence conclusions follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variants and practical forms of Beck's theorem (PTT/meta-note)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beck's theorem has many versions: a weak version with hypotheses on more pairs, an equivalence version (comparison K an equivalence), a constructive version analyzing which hypotheses yield a left adjoint for K or equivalence, and crude versions (VTT/CTT) with strong hypotheses applicable to composites of forgetful functors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text notes these variants and references Barr–Wells (1985) for authoritative definitions of VTT and CTT; exercises in the text explore the different hypotheses and consequences.
